ops.body:
Cleanup executed on the yasyf box (2026-07-25) + scope growth. Evidence file on the box: `/tmp/daemonkit-test-leaks-1785025196.txt` (Section 1 = kill targets with full ps lines, Section 2 = survey of every process referencing a Go test temp dir).

Killed (all PPID 1, UID 501, command line matched): 3× TestBridgeRecoveryReapsLeaderlessGroupBeforeReceiptAcknowledge busy-wait loops (oldest 3d15h, up to 19 min CPU each), 2× TestProcessVerifierCancellationReapsAndReusesDedicatedLane verifier-children (1d20h), 1× TestCmdTransportResetKillsBackgroundedDescendant helper (2d8h, 51 min CPU). Four of six ignored SIGTERM **because the test scripts install `trap '' TERM` deliberately** — TERM→KILL needed. That trap choice is itself part of the bug surface: a leaked helper is unkillable by the polite path.

**Two MORE leaking families found in the survey** (12 procs from a single Jul 23 run, same trap-TERM shape, kill authorized under the same gate): `TestRunCombinedCancellationReapsDaemonizedDescendantAndRecord` (8 procs, 4 parent/child pairs) and `TestRuntimeRetainsOwnershipOnIncompleteWorkerSettlement` (4 procs). Total: **5 distinct kill/reap/settlement tests** whose helpers outlive an externally killed test binary. The fix should be one shared mechanism in the test-helper spawn path (parent-death detection: stdin-pipe-EOF exit convention or kqueue EVFILT_PROC), not per-test patches. Note this overlaps the spawn-gate P1 (task 34996a3b): the leaked scripts' `while [ ! -f …/release ]; do sleep 0.01; done` + `trap '' TERM` preamble is exactly the TERM-immune busy-spin gate that forensics documented.
